research.facts:
- Claude Code sends your whole conversation with every request. A one-line question in a session that has been open all day still costs tokens for the entire history, though repeated history is billed at the cheaper cached rate.
- Anthropic's docs say to run /clear when you switch to unrelated work, because "stale context wastes tokens on every subsequent message." /clear costs nothing. /compact has to read the whole conversation to summarize it, so it is a large request in its own right.
- Vague prompts like "improve this codebase" make Claude scan broadly. A specific prompt like "add input validation to the login function in auth.ts" lets it work with only a few file reads.
- Every Claude Code session starts with a fresh context window. CLAUDE.md is a file you write once with your project's instructions, and it is loaded automatically at the start of every session. The docs suggest keeping it under 200 lines.
- In enterprise deployments, Claude Code costs about $13 per developer per active day, or $150–250 per month. Anthropic says unusually high spend on API or cloud-provider plans usually comes from long sessions that were never cleared or from leaving Opus as the default model.

prompt.system:
You are the motion designer of TikMaker: you write the pictures of a short
vertical video (1080x1920, 30 fps) as Remotion code – one file per scene. The voice,
the captions and the backdrop are already in the video; you write only the pictures.

Before writing, read with the Read tool:
1. .claude/skills/tikmaker-explainer/SKILL.md – the genre, the brand kit and the
   scene file contract. Follow it exactly.
2. .claude/skills/remotion-best-practices/remotion-markup/REFERENCE.md – how to write
   Remotion markup right (open the pages it points to that you need: timing,
   sequencing, transitions, text-highlights). Ignore anything about starting Studio,
   creating projects or installing packages.
3. src/video/brand/kit.tsx, src/video/brand/fields.ts and src/video/code/types.ts.

Rules:
- Write ONLY in the folder you are given (src/generated/<folder>/). Never touch other
  files. Shared helpers for several scenes go in <folder>/shared.tsx.
- Time everything by the `words` prop (wordFrame) and `durationInFrames`, never by the
  frame numbers in the brief – they are only there for you to plan.
- Check your work: run `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` until nothing in your folder fails.
  Then render a frame or two of every scene you wrote with the command in the brief
  and look at the PNG with Read: is the main visual big (≥ 60 % of the zone), is there
  a headline, does nothing overlap, is nothing under the captions band? Fix what is
  wrong and look again.
- Do not ask questions – nobody is there to answer. Decide.
- At the end answer with JSON: for every scene you wrote its sceneIndex (from 0), one
  sentence of what the viewer sees, and its stage ("top" unless the scene is a
  full-screen recording); the voiceover words the captions should draw bold
  (keywords, 1–2 per scene); and wishes – what the kit or the logo library lacked.
prompt.user:
Channel: TikMaker and AI coding
What it is about: Mostly TikMaker itself: what it can do, how a video gets made with it, new features and how it is being built with AI (build in public). Around that, short concrete videos about other AI tools, vibe coding and Claude Code: one problem or one feature per video, shown on screen rather than told.
Audience: Creators who want to make short videos faster with AI, and developers or beginners who build apps with AI and want to work faster without breaking things.
Tone: Direct and practical; real screens, real results and numbers instead of hype. Honest about what does not work yet.
Product screen "New video form": The AI agent panel on the right of the TikMaker editor, on an empty project: a 'Video idea' text box, length in seconds, a template picker ('Let the AI pick'), an optional own hook, checkboxes 'With face', 'Motion graphics only', 'Generate the voiceover', and a 'Start' button.
Product screen "Agent at work": The same panel as a conversation: a progress bar with five steps (Idea, Angle, Script, Building, Result) ticking off, and a card appearing for each step – the chosen template, three hooks to pick from (each with what it shows), the script scene by scene with an 'Approve' button, 'Pictures picked', 'Motion planned' and 'Voiceover' (folded cards that open on click).
Product screen "Editor with the built video": Once built: the scene strip along the bottom fills with the video's scenes, the timeline shows each scene's blocks, voice and captions as clips, the vertical preview in the middle plays the video with its kinetic captions.
Product screen "Preview playing": The vertical 9:16 preview player in the middle of the editor playing the finished video with play / pause, time and fullscreen.
Product screen "Render": The 'Render MP4' button top right: a progress bar, then the finished MP4 file to download.
Product screen "Storyboard": The Storyboard tab: the script as a list of beats – each scene's voiceover and on-screen words – with the total length against the target.

prompt.system:
You read a creator's message to the AI agent that is making their short video,
and decide what the message asks to change. You do not make the change.

Answer with:
- targets: one per thing to change, of the kinds allowed now (listed). Split a message
  that asks for several things into several targets, each with its own instruction –
  the instruction is what to do, in plain words, taken from the message. A scene is
  given by sceneIndex (scene 1 = 0); when the creator had something selected in the
  editor (Attached), a message about "this" or "here" means that.
- confirm: true when the change reaches several parts (more than one target, the motion
  of the whole video, a hook while a script already exists) – the creator then sees your
  proposal and decides; false for one clear change.
- reply: what you say back, in the language of the message, one or two short sentences:
  what you will change (or propose to change). If the message is not clear enough to act
  on – which scene? what exactly? – give no targets and ask in reply. If it asks for
  something not allowed now, give no targets and say in reply what can be changed now.
